keyFindings.description: defer waitIntakes() replaced the old defer that ran cancel() first. waitIntakes is stopIntakes(context.Background()), which waits in running.Wait for settings.Run, Intake.Run and JobIntake.Run, each of which returns only once ctx ends; the only cancel is the defer at main.go:196, which Go runs after this one. A panic in main's goroutine after line 568 (routes.New's mux registrations, newHTTPServer, joinRegistry) therefore hangs the process with the panic unprinted and the bound intake still consuming the durable, until a signal (the probe's kill) cancels ctx; at 0c22dd3f the same panic exited. Fix: defer func() { cancel(); waitIntakes() }().

Intake.Run makes its 15 s stop context only when it reaches the stop, after bind(ctx) returns, and the bind's reconcile and subscribe JetStream calls do not watch ctx (each up to nats.MaxWait 10 s, bus/nats.go:380). A signal during a standby's bind poll that then binds the durable stops at bind end + 15 s. This round removed the outer deadline (intakeStopDeadline, signal + 25 s) and moved waitIntakes before deregister/pool.Close, so that case can push the registry delete and the pool close past stopGrace (30 s), where the kill cuts them; shutdown.go:95-102, intake_delivery.go:77-92 and README.md:703-712 say 15 s after the signal at the latest. Start the budget when ctx ends (e.g. a stop context armed by context.AfterFunc(ctx, ...)), or correct the claim and restore a bound.

Cleanup, not a gate: DrainSubscription, the draining flag and Release are always called in sequence by one caller (intake_delivery.go:137,171); DrainSubscription could give up the registration itself and drop the flag and both recovery checks.

Cleanup, not a gate: StartIntakes' stop(ctx) and its give-up AfterFunc are a mode only TestAHandlerTheStopGivesUpIsRedeliveredAtOnce uses now that main passes context.Background(); the docs at intakes.go:36-39 and intake_delivery.go:113-116 still describe it. The fix for the stop budget above may settle it.
